metadata.note: The Providence, Warren and Bristol Railroad (Providence - Bristol, RI, opened 12 July 1855) and its Fall River branch (the Fall River, Warren and Providence, Warren - Fall River, opened 1865, bridged to Fall River 1875), drawn from 1860 by operating company: PW&B 1860-1891, Old Colony 1891-1893, New Haven 1893-1937 [OPEN] on the Bristol line; Old Colony 1875-1893 and New Haven 1893-1932 on the Fall River branch. The 1855-1860 era, when the Boston and Providence operated the line, is already drawn as bp-providence-warren-bristol in boston_and_providence_railroad.geojson and is not repeated. Features split at every operator change (Rule 4) and, within the New Haven era, at electrification (mode change, steam intercity_rail -> electric commuter_rail) and at the 15/16 Nov 1908 move from India Point to Union Station via the East Side Tunnel (alignment change, Rule 2). Research report: research/branches/providence_warren_and_bristol_railroad.txt.

not_yet_sourced: END OF BRISTOL PASSENGER SERVICE [OPEN]: drawn to 1937, the last confirmed year (AR, TrailLink, dated Apr 1937 forum photo). 1938 (AR, WEST, RIR 'about', Fowler, forum: 21 Sep 1938 hurricane) is asserted without a dated train. A Providence Journal / Bristol Phoenix last-train story or a RI PUC discontinuance order would settle it. Do not extend without evidence.
End of electric operation on the Bristol line: 1934 (WPWB, WCPB, WEBBP, RIR) vs 1937 (AR) vs 1938 (Fowler). Drawn as a 1934 equipment change inside continuous service.
Electrification year: 1900 (WPWB, WFRWP) vs 1901 (Fowler). Era boundary inside continuous service; 1900 drawn.

Fall River branch 1865-1875 operator (PW&B briefly then FRW&P, per WFRWP, vs the B&P from 1872/73 per WPWB and the WFRWP infobox) and the Old Colony takeover year (1873 WPWB vs 1875 WFRWP). Karr 2017 pp.165-169 or the 1911 RI RRC report p.428 would settle it.
Whether through Providence - Fall River trains ran 1875-1891 across the PW&B / Old Colony boundary at Warren, and under whose name.

Whether the Boston and Providence (owner 1872-1888) or the Old Colony (controlling through its 1888 B&P lease) ran Bristol trains in its own name before the 1 July 1891 lease. Drawn as PW&B 1860-1891.
Exact 1860 start of PW&B operation (year only).
Pre-1908 Providence terminal: India Point vs Fowler's 'Providence (Fox Point)' (1904) - treated as the same India Street/India Point terminal area; no separate Fox Point station located.
Where Fall River branch trains terminated in Fall River (Bowenville vs the Fall River depot). Drawn only to the branch's junction with the Fall River line.
Route of the 1908 connection between the Crook Point bridge and Boston Switch: drawn on OHM's 1835 B&P East Junction roadbed (assumed).
Mileage: 14.1 mi (WPWB / 1911 RRC) vs 15.7 mi Fox Point - Bristol (Fowler) vs 13.7 mi traced India Point - Bristol.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate; no timetable with frequencies or running times was read.
omitted_blocks: [0] Boston and Providence operation 1855-1860 - already drawn as bp-providence-warren-bristol in boston_and_providence_railroad.geojson; not duplicated.

[7] Fall River, Warren and Providence, Warren - Brayton Point (ferry to Fall River), 1865-1875 - omitted: the operating company is unresolved (PW&B / FRW&P / B&P / Old Colony conflict between WFRWP text, WFRWP infobox and WPWB) and no Fowler letter earlier than 1894 is on the branch; the report recommends omission until Karr or the 1911 RRC report settles it.

[11] Bristol street-running extension, Bristol station - Church St - Constitution St (c.0.5 mi, Fowler a 1904 / b 1920 only) - omitted: whose streetcar track it was is unknown and the span rests on two Fowler letters [OPEN] both ends; short enough that it adds nothing visible.

[12] Electric cars to Providence Union Station over streetcar track via the Washington Avenue bridge, 1901-c.1902 - omitted: single source (Fowler line 81 note), [ANCHOR] 1901 only, track owner unknown, and the streetcar route is not traced.

[13] Post-1938 excursions and chartered fan trips on the Bristol line (WPWB, WEST) - omitted: drawable NONE, no trip is dated or routed. Narragansett Park race trains ran on the East Junction Branch, not this road.
metadata.mode_rule7: The New Haven's 1900-1934 electric operation (600 V DC trolley wire, trolley poles, converted heavy-rail coaches, steam freight on the same track) is drawn commuter_rail, not interurban: Rule 7 tests what the line was BUILT for, and these were steam railroads built 1855/1865 and later electrified by their steam-road owner, like the NH's other electrified branches. CONFLICT recorded: the WFRWP infobox labels the line 'Interurban (1900-1934)' and WPWB says it 'operated similarly to an interurban'. Steam eras are intercity_rail, matching bp-providence-warren-bristol. The 1934-1937 gas-electric cars stay commuter_rail on the same feature.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn (Rule 1): the Bristol line after passengers ended (1937/38) to the Penn Central abandonment of Warren - Bristol (1973) and later cut-backs (1976, 2006); the Fall River branch Warren - Brayton 1932-1937 and the Warren - East Warren stub to 1976; the Bold Point / Wilkesbarre Pier spur; the B&P Seekonk Branch. The P&W East Providence Branch's 1893-1896 passengers are drawn in providence_and_worcester_railroad.geojson, not here.
metadata.horsecar: Rule 5: 1855-1857 passenger cars were horse-hauled from India Point across Providence to the P&W depot (WPWB). That city leg is not drawn in any era; all features start at the India Point terminal or, from 1908, Union Station by the tunnel.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 13.7 mi India Point - Bristol against c.15.7 mi documented Fox Point - Bristol (Fowler line 81) and 14.1 mi (WPWB, 1911 RI Railroad Commissioners' report, probably measured from the East Providence junction). Geometry is copied programmatically, vertex for vertex, from feature bp-providence-warren-bristol in boston_and_providence_railroad.geojson (not re-traced): India Point - Boston Switch (about 0.2 mi, including the India Point bridge, gone) is OpenHistoricalMap ways -200075066/-200075067 (1849 map) and the remaining ~13.5 mi is the East Bay Bike Path, which keeps within 150 m of OHM's 1887/1890 USGS trace of the PW&B (OHM -200053746, -200484424). No straight-line leg. The ~2 mi shortfall against Fowler is unresolved; most likely Fowler measures from a different Providence station point. TERMINAL: drawn from the India Point terminal at the west end of the India Point bridge. Fowler names the pre-1908 terminal 'Providence (PWB)' (1893/96) and 'Providence (Fox Point)' (1904); India Point is the southern tip of the Fox Point district and the PW&B depot was on India Street there, so any difference between the 'India Point' and 'Fox Point' terminals is a few hundred metres at most and is not drawn separately - no source located a distinct Fox Point station. The horse-hauled city leg India Point - P&W depot (to 1857) is not drawn (Rule 5). ALIGNMENT: this is the pre-1908 India Point bridge route, correct for its era; Fowler notes trains first reversed at Boston Switch until a west-to-south curve was installed (c.1890?) - the drawn line takes the curve throughout.

segments.note: Providence, Warren and Bristol Railroad running its own trains, India Point (Providence) - East Providence - Riverside - Barrington - Warren - Bristol. Start 1860 is approximate (no month): the year the PW&B began using its own locomotives after the Boston and Providence had operated the line from its 12 July 1855 opening (WPWB citing Karr 2017; the 1855-1860 era is drawn as bp-providence-warren-bristol). End 1 July 1891, the 99-year lease to the Old Colony (WPWB citing The Story of the Old Colony Railroad, 1919). Fowler's 1876 Pathfinder letter (y) on Nayatt, Barrington, Warren, Bristol, Riverside, Silver Spring confirms passenger stops mid-era. OWNERSHIP CAVEAT, not drawn as a split: the B&P bought the PW&B in 1872 and the Old Colony controlled it 1888-1891 through its lease of the B&P (WPWB, RIR) - nothing seen says either ran the Bristol trains in its own name before 1891 (report UNRESOLVED 9). Headway 120 min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: dates and operator from the research report block [1]: WPWB (Karr 2017 pp.165-169; The Story of the Old Colony Railroad 1919) for the c.1860 start and the 1 Jul 1891 lease; Fowler line 81 letter y (1876) for mid-era stops. Start year approximate. Headway not sourced.

Start 1900 per WPWB and WFRWP - CONFLICT: Fowler gives 1901. Fowler's 1904 letter (a) is on every station including 'Providence (Fox Point)'. Ends 15/16 November 1908 when the East Side Tunnel opened and the trains moved to Union Station (WEST gives both dates) - a route change, continued as nh-providence-bristol-tunnel. Headway 30 min is an estimate: WPWB says peak headways were PROJECTED at 8-10 min and AR says 'about 100 trains daily' at peak (undated); neither is a timetable.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-17), ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H (East Providence Branch 1130186138/1416656152, East Side Tunnel 1416656151, Crook Point viaduct 1416654982/-983 and bascule 601799841, disused 185319879), OHM way -200075065 (B&P 1835), routed with opstrace.py; Boston Switch - Bristol copied from bp-providence-warren-bristol.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 15.5 mi Providence Union Station - Bristol (no documented figure for the post-1908 route found; 14.1 mi in the 1911 RRC report via WPWB is probably East Providence - Bristol, and 15.7 mi Fowler is Fox Point - Bristol). NEW 1908 ALIGNMENT, drawn deliberately (Rule 2): from the 15/16 Nov 1908 opening of the East Side Tunnel the Bristol trains ran Union Station - East Side Tunnel - Crook Point Bascule Bridge - East Providence, not over the India Point bridge, so this feature does NOT reuse the India Point head of the pre-1908 features. Head, about 2.1 mi, traced with opstrace.py from OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H: East Providence Branch (abandoned) from the old Union Station track area (41.8267, -71.4127; the 1898 station's platforms, not today's 1986 station on the relocated NEC) 0.2 mi to the west portal, East Side Tunnel (disused) 1.0 mi, the Crook Point viaduct/bascule bridge ways (disused) and a disused way 0.2 mi south to where it meets the OHM 1835 Boston and Providence way -200075065; then 0.4 mi along that OHM way SW to Boston Switch - an ASSUMPTION that the 1908 connection used the old B&P East Junction roadbed there (the OSM disused way ends on it, within 20 m), not separately sourced. From Boston Switch to Bristol (about 13.5 mi) the geometry is copied programmatically from bp-providence-warren-bristol (East Bay Bike Path / OHM), as the pre-1908 features. No straight-line leg. The Bristol street-running extension to Church St / Constitution St (report block [11]) is not drawn.

segments.note: New Haven electric service from Providence Union Station through the East Side Tunnel (5,080 ft, Benefit St - Gano St) and over the Crook Point Bascule Bridge to East Providence and the original PW&B line to Bristol, from the tunnel's opening on 15/16 November 1908 (WEST, WCPB). Fowler's 1920 letter (b) is on every station. Some Bristol trains street-ran on streetcar track beyond the Bristol station to Church St and Constitution St (WPWB, Fowler) - not drawn. Electric operation ended 1934 (WPWB, WCPB, WEBBP; RIR: 'cut-back in 1932 and ended in 1934') - CONFLICT: AR has electric operation to 1937, Fowler 'electrified 1901 > 1938'. 1934 is a change of equipment, not an end of service; continued by the next segment. Headway 30 min is an estimate (WPWB's 8-10 min peak headways were projected, not timetabled).
sources: Segment-level: dates from the research report block [5]: WEST and WCPB (15/16 Nov 1908 opening), WPWB, WCPB, WEBBP and RIR (electric to 1934; AR 1937 and Fowler 1938 conflict recorded), Fowler line 81 (b, 1920). Headway estimated, not sourced.

segments.note: Gas-electric cars replaced the electric service in 1934 (WPWB; start approximate) and ran Providence - Bristol over the same tunnel route. END IS [OPEN]: 1937 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. 1937 is placed inside service by AR (gas-electric 'in 1937'), TrailLink via WEBBP ('All passenger service was discontinued in 1937') and a forum photo dated 12 April 1937 of NH car 9110 on Thames Street, Bristol (OGR, forum-grade); WPWB's 'entirely ceased by 1937' is compatible. 1938 is asserted by AR ('completely discontinued by 1938' after the 21 Sep 1938 hurricane), WEST ('All passenger services ceased in 1938'), RIR ('until about 1938'), Fowler ('> 1938') and the forum poster, but none dates a 1938 train. No primary source (timetable, last-train story, PUC order) was found. Do not extend to 1938 without evidence. Freight continued after passengers ended (Warren - Bristol abandoned 1973), and undated excursions / fan trips used the line later (WPWB, WEST) - none drawn. Headway 90 min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: dates from the research report block [6]: WPWB (gas-electric 1934, ceased by 1937), WEBBP/TrailLink (ended 1937), AR (gas-electric 1937; ended by 1938), WEST (ceased 1938), RIR (about 1938), Fowler line 81 (> 1938). Secondary sources only, in conflict; end [OPEN]. Headway not sourced.

Same geometry for all three branch features (no alignment change 1875-1932 found).

segments.note: Old Colony operation of the Fall River, Warren and Providence's line, Warren - Touisset - South Swansea - Somerset - Brayton - Slade's Ferry Bridge - Fall River, from the opening of Slade's Ferry Bridge in 1875 (WSFB, WFRWP: 'The Old Colony Railroad operated the line from 1875 until 1891 when it bought it outright') to the New Haven's lease of the Old Colony in 1893. CONFLICT on the OC takeover: WPWB says the B&P sold the branch to the OC in 1873; WFRWP's 1875 is drawn, and 1873-1875 (a ferry-connected stub to Brayton Point) is left undrawn with the unresolved 1865-1875 era. Through Providence - Fall River trains are plausible but undocumented for 1875-1891 (the Bristol line was PW&B, the branch OC). Fowler's 1893/96 letter (z) is on South Swansea, Brayton, Brayton Point and Cole's. Headway 180 min is an estimate, not sourced.

properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org, 2026-10-17) ways -200484460, -200484459, -200498920, -200498918 ('Fall River, Warren and Providence Railroad'), cross-checked against OSM railway=abandoned old_railway_operator=NYNH&H ways in Swansea/Somerset; routed with opstrace.py.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 7.6 mi Warren (junction with the Bristol line) - Fall River (junction with the Old Colony Fall River line south of Bowenville) against c.7.8 mi documented (Fowler line 82, Warren 11.6 -> 19.4) and 8 mi (WFRWP); about 3% short, plausibly because the drawn end is the junction rather than the Fall River station. Traced with opstrace.py over OpenHistoricalMap ways named 'Fall River, Warren and Providence Railroad' (-200484460, -200484459, -200498920 = Slade's Ferry Bridge, end_date 1970, -200498918; USGS-era 1888/1890), which agree within 3-33 m with OSM railway=abandoned ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H through Swansea and Somerset (1232265173/-174/-177, 1414292161, 199428386, 1232265171). The west end meets the Bristol line within 3 m of its drawn geometry at Warren. No straight-line leg. Slade's Ferry Bridge (1875, rail on the upper deck) was demolished c.1970; its drawn line is OHM geometry only. The drawn Fall River end is the OHM junction at 41.7168, -71.1523, not Bowenville station (Nominatim's Bowenville hamlet centroid is ~1 km north); where branch trains terminated in Fall River is not established in the report and is not drawn. Same geometry for all three branch features (no alignment change 1875-1932 found).

segments.note: New Haven electric service on the Fall River branch, Fall River - Warren with through cars to Providence, from electrification in 1900 (WFRWP, WPWB - CONFLICT: Fowler 1901) until January 1932, when a passing ship struck and disabled Slade's Ferry Bridge (WFRWP; WPWB 'ceased after a ship struck ... in 1932'; Fowler '1901 > 1932'). 1932 holds only a few January weeks. The bridge was not rebuilt for rail and buses replaced the trains (WFRWP) - the buses are not drawn. Freight continued Warren - Brayton until ICC abandonment permission in 1937 (Boston Globe 11 Jun 1937 via WFRWP) and on a Warren - East Warren stub to 1976 - not drawn (Rule 1); no source claims passenger trains to Brayton after the bridge strike. Fowler letters a (1904) and b (1920) on the branch stations. Headway 60 min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: dates from the research report block [10]: WFRWP (electrification 1900; bridge strike January 1932; buses), WPWB, WSFB, Fowler line 82 (a, b; 1901 > 1932). Headway not sourced.
